exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Function

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{(4x+7)^2}$ is defined for $x > -\dfrac{7}{4}.$ Find $f^{-1}(x).$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{1}{(4x+7)^2} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{1}{(4y+7)^2}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{1}{(4y+7)^2} \\[5pt] x(4y+7)^2 &= 1 \\[5pt] (4y+7)^2 &= \dfrac{1}{x} \\[5pt] \sqrt{(4y+7)^2} &= \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{x}} \\[5pt] |4y+7| &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\[5pt] 4y +7 &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\[5pt] 4y &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} - 7 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{x}} - \dfrac{7}{4} \end{align}

Note that we used the fact that for $y > -\dfrac{7}{4},$ we have \[ |4y+7| = 4y+7. \]

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{x}} - \dfrac{7}{4}}. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{5}{6x+2}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{5}{6x+2} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{5}{6y+2}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{5}{6y+2} \\[5pt] x(6y + 2) &= 5 \\[5pt] 6xy + 2x &= 5 \\[5pt] 6xy &= 5 - 2x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{5 - 2x}{6x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{5 - 2x}{6x}}. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{2}{7-5x}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{2}{7-5x} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{2}{7-5y}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{2}{7-5y} \\[5pt] x(7-5y) &= 2 \\[5pt] 7x - 5xy &= 2 \\[5pt] -5xy &= 2 - 7x \\[5pt] 5xy &= 7x - 2 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{7x-2}{5x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{7x-2}{5x}}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Simple Rational Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3x+1}{x-4} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3y+1}{y-4}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3y+1}{y-4} \\[5pt] x(y-4) &= 3y+1 \\[5pt] xy - 4x &= 3y+1 \\[5pt] xy - 3y &= 4x+ 1 \\[5pt] y(x-3) &= 4x + 1 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{4x+1}{x-3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4x+1}{x-3}. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = -\dfrac{2x-5}{x-4}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = -\dfrac{2x-5}{x-4} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = -\dfrac{2y-5}{y-4}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= -\dfrac{2y-5}{y-4} \\[5pt] -x & = \dfrac{2y-5}{y-4} \\[5pt] -x(y-4) &= 2y-5 \\[5pt] -xy + 4x &= 2y-5 \\[5pt] 4x + 5 &= xy + 2y\\[5pt] 4x + 5 &=y(x+2) \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{4x+5}{x+2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \bbox[5pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue} \dfrac{4x+5}{x+2}}. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Simple Rational Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = -\dfrac{x-8}{5x+1} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = -\dfrac{y-8}{5y+1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= -\dfrac{y-8}{5y+1} \\[5pt] -x &= \dfrac{y-8}{5y+1} \\[5pt] -x(5y+1) &= y - 8 \\[5pt] - 5xy -x &= y - 8 \\[5pt] 8 - x &= 5xy + y \\[5pt] 8 - x &= y(5x +1) \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{8 - x}{5x +1} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{8 - x}{5x+1}. \]

\[ y =\dfrac{2x-1}{x+3} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{2y-1}{y+3}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{2y-1}{y+3} \\[5pt] x(y+3) &= 2y-1\\[5pt] xy + 3x &= 2y-1\\[5pt] 3x+1 &=2y-xy \\[5pt] 3x+1 &=y(2- x)\\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3x+1}{2-x} \end{align}

\[ y = \dfrac{5 - 2x}{x+1} \]

\[ x = \dfrac{5- 2y}{y+1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{5 - 2y}{y+1} \\[5pt] x(y+1) &= 5 - 2y \\[5pt] xy + x &= 5 - 2y \\[5pt] xy + 2y &= 5 - x \\[5pt] y(x+2) &= 5 - x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{5-x}{x+2} \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Rational Function

question.text: The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac{2x+k}{x-1}, \qquad x\neq 1 \] has an inverse function given by \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x-8}{x-2}, \qquad x\neq 2. \] What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{2x+k}{x-1} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{2y+k}{y-1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{2y+k}{y-1} \\[5pt] x(y-1) &= 2y + k \\[5pt] xy - x &= 2y + k \\[5pt] xy - 2y &= x + k \\[5pt] y(x-2) &= x+k \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{x + k}{x-2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x + k}{x-2}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-8.$

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{3k}{6+4x}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{9 - 6x}{4x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3k}{6+4x} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3k}{6+4y}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3k}{6+4y} \\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{3k}{6+4y} \\[5pt] x(6+4y) &= 3k \\[5pt] 6x + 4xy &= 3k \\[5pt] 4xy &= 3k - 6x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3k - 6x}{4x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3k - 6x}{4x}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3}.$

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{7x + k}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1 +3x}{7x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{1}{7x + k} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{1}{7y + k}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{1}{7y + k} \\[5pt] x(7y + k) &= 1 \\[5pt] 7xy + kx &= 1 \\[5pt] 7xy &= 1 -kx \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1- kx}{7x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1 -kx}{7x}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-3.$

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{3}{kx-2}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3+2x}{5x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3}{kx-2} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3}{ky-2}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3}{ky-2} \\[5pt] x(ky-2) &= 3 \\[5pt] kxy - 2x &= 3 \\[5pt] kxy &= 3 + 2x\\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3+2x}{kx} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3 + 2x}{kx}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=5.$

question.text: The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac{3-kx}{x+1}, \qquad x\neq -1 \] has an inverse function given by \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3-x}{x+4}, \qquad x\neq -4. \] What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3-kx}{x+1} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3-ky}{y+1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3-ky}{y+1} \\[5pt] x(y +1) &=3 - ky \\[5pt] xy + x &= 3 - ky \\[5pt] xy + ky &= 3 - x \\[5pt] y(x+ k) &= 3 - x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3 - x}{x + k} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3-x}{x + k}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=4.$
